title: Coordinate geometry: distance, slope, and loci

runs.text: Work in a Euclidean coordinate plane with perpendicular axes at the same scale. Let
A locus is the full set of points satisfying a stated geometric or algebraic condition.

Coordinate formulas translate Euclidean length, direction, and incidence into equations. A useful locus argument proves both directions: every geometric point satisfies the equation, and every point satisfying the equation has the required geometry.
. The locus equidistant from two distinct points is their perpendicular bisector.
